reviews.review: I do not think I would have paid for this game, but I got it for free and to be honest it was surprisingly a great fun fighting through the campaigns. It is a simple game in a great universe, where you have to slaughter tons of Orcs and Chaos troopers in many ways. Deffinitely worth to try it.

Speaking only for the single player and only for 2 or so hours worth of content so far: As a personal opinion I cannot recommend this.

The good parts first: It looks very authentic to what the 40k experience should be IMO (only have limited experience of the IP ), the action itself also looks quite nice, the characters themselves both orcs and non also well done and it sounds just what I would have expected.

The bad: WHY DOES THE GAMEPLAY FEEL SO SLUGGISH?? Seriously, melee again looks awesome and even feels so most of the time but then you get bigger orcs and realise that mashing the melee attack button isn't enough and being forced to use a grenade or just kite the bastard looks and feels absurd. As far as I can tell so far you don't have any way to block attacks in melee and even dodge rolling isn't either far or fast enough to escape those bruisers hits so have fun kitting.

And speaking of melee, why don't your comrades actually engage in it? I haven't see either of them ever go melee, they just stand and shoot and even that they do poorly. I bring this up because having played Republic Commando years ago and even 1 or 2 more recent shooter titles my expectations for NPC teammates is a bit higher than meatshields with poor aiming.

Oh and somewhat going back to melee. Why do you recover health by executions? No seriously why? Are health packs or healing stations nonexistent in 40k ( genuine question ). I mean it felt great at first to finish a stunned orc by chainsaw but practically speaking this design choice is IMO rather poorly thought out.
Firstly you still take damage when going in the animation so if you still have a lot of enemies around they can bring you down before the heal kicks-in (At least that's what I saw once happen).
And secondly this method isn't useful if you are facing ranged enemies. There is a secondary way to recover health which I think also applies to ranged attacks and that is to use your rage mechanic. I don't really have any complaints or praise for it, it's there and it works how it's supposed to.

I think one of the reasons why gameplay feels weird is because IMO they tried to balance melee and ranged both and failed to make either one excellent. The melee feels awkward with no block or a better dodge while the range doesn't have the satisfaction you get in melee and you run out or bullets relatively fast if you don't also use melee. Also because you can't heal in ranged without using you rage it makes exchanges less desirable. Or in other words you could think that both systems aren't fully matured yet, they are functional for the most part but feel either incomplete or lackluster. It's rather annoying since I want to like the game but a video game should fundamentally be fun to play IMO unless you are intentionally going for something that might hinder gameplay but add to the atmosphere, story or what have you. And thats fine ultimately but then don't complain if some players who aren't gripped by the story or atmosphere don't stay for a gimped gameplay experience.


I will still mostly try to advance in the campaign but for now this is my impression.

If you are thinking of buying this for the single player IMO there are better shooters out there unless you are very into 40k in which case the looks, sounds and atmosphere might just be enough for you. As for multiplayer I have no comment thus far. Haven't tried it nor plan to.
